title: First-group metadata may store a shared optimizer counter
applies_when: An optimizer property setter returns after its first parameter group, and a proposed bug assumes every group must store an equal step key.
lesson: Trace the property's getter and schedule consumers before demanding per-group key equality. TorchAO PruneOptimizer stores its shared num_steps on the first regularized group; initialization/checkpoint defaults use that location, and each group's sparsity ramp reads self.num_steps rather than its own group key. Multiple regularized groups alone therefore do not establish a desynchronized schedule. Seek an observable wrong consumer result before changing storage semantics or writing an all-keys-equal regression.
avoid_when: Other optimizers can genuinely require per-group counters. A consumer that reads group['num_steps'], a documented per-group serialization contract, parameter-group mutation or changed code can invalidate this inference. Source and extracted-method behavior do not establish full TorchAO training, distributed checkpoint or numerical correctness. Do not automatically discard a new counterexample.

evidence.note: Pinned source shows the first-group getter/setter/deleter, first-group checkpoint default and _effective_min_sparsity reading the shared self.num_steps. This refutes the key-inequality-implies-schedule-divergence inference, not every optimizer defect.
